versions.name: Classic Definition
versions.description: H1 → Definition heading → highlighted definition card → explanation paragraph
versions.definition: A variable is a name that refers to an object so that the program can access that object.
versions.explanation: In Python, assignment binds a name to an object. The name can later be rebound to another object.

versions.name: Definition + Key Characteristics
versions.definition: A Python variable is a name used to reference an object during program execution.
versions.explanation: Understanding these characteristics helps explain assignment, reassignment, identity, and object behavior.

characteristics.title: Name
characteristics.description: A variable provides a readable name for a reference.

characteristics.title: Reference
characteristics.description: The name refers to an object rather than acting as a fixed storage box.

characteristics.title: Dynamic Binding
characteristics.description: A name can be rebound to another object.

characteristics.title: Object Identity
characteristics.description: The referenced object has its own identity.

characteristics.title: Scope
characteristics.description: The meaning and lifetime of a name depend on its scope.

versions.name: Definition + Real-World Analogy
versions.description: Definition → technical explanation → real-world analogy card
versions.definition: A variable can be understood as a name associated with an object.
versions.explanation: The name provides a convenient way for code to refer to the object without repeatedly describing the object itself.

analogy.title: Real-World Analogy
analogy.description: Think of a labeled locker. The label helps you identify which locker you mean; changing the label's association does not mean the label itself becomes the locker.

versions.name: Definition + Why It Matters
versions.description: Definition → explanation → Why is this important?
versions.definition: A variable gives a program a reusable name through which an object can be accessed.
versions.explanation: Variables make programs easier to read, reason about, and modify because values or objects can be referred to by meaningful names.
versions.whyItMatters: Without meaningful names, programs would be much harder to express and maintain. Naming lets later statements refer to data without repeating the original construction.

versions.name: Definition + Visual Concept
versions.description: Definition → short explanation → infographic / visual model
versions.definition: A Python variable name refers to an object.
versions.explanation: The simplest mental model is a name connected to an object. The object has its own value and identity.

versions.name: Definition + Technical Breakdown
versions.description: Definition → terminology → technical explanation → key points
versions.definition: In Python, assignment binds a name to an object within a namespace.
versions.explanation: This terminology gives a more precise model than treating a Python variable as a simple memory box.

terminology.description: Mapping in which names are associated with objects.
Runtime entity with identity, type, and value.
Association between a name and an object.

versions.name: Complete Learning Card
versions.description: Definition → explanation → characteristics → visual → example → key takeaway
versions.definition: A Python variable is a name that refers to an object.
versions.explanation: This complete presentation combines the conceptual, technical, visual, and practical views into one learning card.

characteristics.title: Identity

versions.takeaway: Think in terms of names, objects, and bindings rather than treating a Python variable as a fixed box containing a value.
